passage: Anders came back from the toilet to find his rocket drawing torn in two. Emil stood beside it, chewing his sleeve. Heat rushed through Anders's whole body and he punched Emil's arm. Emil yelled and hit back, and both boys were crying when Mamma came in. "Hands are not for hitting. Tell Emil with words." Anders gulped. "You tore my rocket and I am so mad!" "I did not mean to," Emil sniffed. Mamma fetched the tape while both boys sat glaring, a bit red-eyed.

qa.q: What did Anders find torn in two?
qa.a: He found his rocket drawing torn in two.

qa.q: What was Anders feeling when he punched Emil's arm?
qa.a: He was furious. The anger rushed through his whole body and he lashed out before words came.

qa.q: What worked better than hitting once Mamma came in?
qa.a: Saying with words, "You tore my rocket and I am so mad," got a hearing, and Mamma fetched tape to fix it. Hitting only made Emil angry and he hit back.

qa.q: How might Emil see the torn drawing and Anders's punch?
qa.a: Emil says he did not mean to, so he may feel guilty and hurt at being hit. He hit back because he was scared and upset too.

grounding: My sibling broke my drawing and I hit back; a wise child says you broke it, I am mad, and gets help.

passage: At the community centre art class, Chaitanya had drawn a big blue rocket. His sister Vidya reached across for the glue and tore it in half. Chaitanya's whole body went hot. He hit her arm. Vidya howled and hit him back. The art teacher came over. "Hands are not for hitting. Chaitanya, sit on the calm mat for a bit." From the mat, Chaitanya watched Vidya rub her arm and glare at him. Later the teacher knelt beside him. "Next time, try saying, 'You broke it, I'm mad,' and call me."

qa.a: Chaitanya had drawn a big blue rocket.

qa.q: How did Chaitanya feel when his rocket was torn?
qa.a: He felt so angry that his whole body went hot, and he hit Vidya before thinking.

qa.q: What could Chaitanya say next time instead of hitting?
qa.a: He could say "You broke it, I'm mad" and call the teacher, so the problem gets fixed without anyone being hurt.

qa.q: How does Vidya probably feel after being hit?
qa.a: She feels hurt and angry too, which is why she hits back and glares at her brother.

grounding: A young boy hits his sister after she tears his drawing, faces a consequence, and is taught to name his anger and get help.

passage:
Monday: Yamini spilled juice on Sarita's rainbow drawing. Sarita's fists shook and she smacked her sister's back. Yamini cried and threw a crayon at her. Amma sent them both to separate rooms. Sarita kicked the door, still hot all over.
Tuesday: Amma and Sarita practised: "You broke it, I am mad." Sarita said it loudly, stamping her foot.
Thursday: Yamini tore the corner of Sarita's new picture. Sarita's hands balled up. Then she shouted, "You tore it! I'm mad! Amma!" Amma came with the tape.

qa.q: What did Yamini spill on Monday?
qa.a: Yamini spilled juice on Sarita's rainbow drawing.

qa.q: How can you tell Sarita's anger filled her whole body?
qa.a: Her fists shook, she smacked her sister and kicked the door, still hot all over.

qa.q: What changed on Thursday, and why was it better?
qa.a: Sarita used her words and called Amma instead of hitting, so the picture got fixed and no one was hurt. 👍

qa.q: How might Yamini feel on Monday after being smacked?
qa.a: She feels hurt and angry, so she throws a crayon back and the fight grows.

grounding: Over a few days, a young girl who hit her sister for spoiling her drawing learns to name her anger and call for help.
